title: Canonical Order and the Case of Peter
english: By Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria.
1. On a deposed bishop also ceasing from sacred ministry.

When each of our affairs moves straight along the path of canonical good order, it stirs up no turmoil for us; it also frees us from the slanders of some, and, better still, wins us the good word of right-minded people. For who would not welcome an impartial verdict, whomever it may concern? Or how could judging rightly and lawfully be anything but beyond reproach, or rather full of every praise? I write this now because your piety, in the letters you sent to me and to our most holy and most God-beloved brother and fellow bishop Proclus, calls the most reverent and most God-fearing Peter a bishop, while he weeps and says that he has been removed without reason from the church assigned to him.
It would have been consistent either for him to hold the name of the priesthood together with its reality, or at least, if he truly deserved not to preside at the divine altar, not even…
translator_notes: Copy-text: the Greek of PG 77 (Khazarzar transcription).
The heading line renders the Latin edition title, Epistula canonica ad Domnum.
ΤΟΥ ΕΝ ΑΓΙΟΙΣ ('of the one among the saints') is rendered 'By Saint Cyril'; no 'our father' is supplied because the Greek does not have πατρὸς ἡμῶν.

Heading 1: περὶ τοῦ ἐπίσκοπον καθαιρεθέντα καὶ τοῦ ἱερουργεῖν παύεσθαι. The first τοῦ governs the infinitive παύεσθαι, with ἐπίσκοπον καθαιρεθέντα as its subject and τοῦ ἱερουργεῖν as the genitive of separation; καί is 'also'. Rendered 'On a deposed bishop also ceasing from sacred ministry'.
εὐθὺ φέρωνται κανονικῆς εὐταξίας: εὐθύ with the genitive means 'straight toward'; rendered 'moves straight along the path of canonical good order'.
ψῆφον ἀπροσκλινῆ, ἥπερ ἂν γένοιτο περί τινων: 'an impartial verdict, whomever it may concern'.

θεοσέβεια ('your piety') is a form of address for a fellow bishop; ὁσιώτατος / θεοφιλέστατος are rendered 'most holy' / 'most God-beloved', εὐλαβέστατος / θεοσεβέστατος 'most reverent' / 'most God-fearing'.
The letters were sent to Cyril and to Proclus (of Constantinople); Peter is the bishop whom Domnus still names a bishop although he was removed from his see.
εἴπερ ἦν ἄξιος τοῦ μὴ προεστάναι θείου θυσιαστηρίου: the negation sits on the infinitive, 'if he truly deserved not to preside at the divine altar', that is, deserved removal.

The section ends mid-sentence at μηδ' αὐτῇ; the sentence continues in the next section with τιμᾶσθαι τῇ κλήσει τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς ('to be honored with the very title of bishop'), where αὐτῇ ('the very') is rendered.
